title: Catalyst System Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
plain: The computer thinks the catalytic converter on bank 1 is not cleaning the exhaust as well as it should.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
Rotten egg smell in some cases

causes.name: Exhaust leak near the oxygen sensors
Engine misfire or oil burning that damaged the converter

checks: Scan for misfire and fuel trim codes first and fix those
Check for exhaust leaks near the oxygen sensors
Compare upstream and downstream O2 sensor readings
fix: Most often a new catalytic converter, but rule out O2 sensors and exhaust leaks first.
examples: Often seen on high-mileage Toyota Camry, Honda Accord and Chevrolet Silverado
drive: It usually doesn't change how the car drives, so book a repair, though it may fail an emissions test. If the check engine light is flashing, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off.
test_first: Check for misfires, exhaust leaks and oil burning, and verify both oxygen sensor readings before replacing the converter. Fix the root cause first or a new converter can fail too.
urgent_if: If the check engine light is flashing or the engine is shaking hard, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. Don't keep driving; a heavy misfire can overheat and ruin the catalytic converter and leave you without power in traffic. Have it towed or checked right away.

title: Warm Up Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
plain: The small catalytic converter close to the engine on bank 1, which does most of the cleaning right after a cold start, is not working as well as it should.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Exhaust leak near the oxygen sensors
Misfire or oil burning that damaged the converter

checks: Scan for misfire and fuel trim codes first and fix those
Check for exhaust leaks near the oxygen sensors
Compare upstream and downstream O2 sensor readings
fix: Usually a new front (warm-up) catalytic converter, after ruling out sensors and exhaust leaks.
drive: It usually doesn't change how the car drives, so book a repair, though it may fail an emissions test. If the check engine light is flashing, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off.
test_first: Check for misfires, exhaust leaks and oil burning, and verify both oxygen sensor readings before replacing the converter. Fix the root cause first or a new converter can fail too.
urgent_if: If the check engine light is flashing or the engine is shaking hard, pull over when it's safe and turn the engine off. Don't keep driving; a heavy misfire can overheat and ruin the catalytic converter and leave you without power in traffic. Have it towed or checked right away.

title: Main Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
plain: The main catalytic converter on bank 1 is not cleaning the exhaust as well as it should.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Exhaust leak near the oxygen sensors
Engine misfire or oil burning that damaged the converter

checks: Scan for misfire and fuel trim codes first and fix those
Check for exhaust leaks near the oxygen sensors
Compare upstream and downstream O2 sensor readings
fix: Usually a new catalytic converter, after ruling out sensors and exhaust leaks.

title: Heated Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
plain: Some vehicles have an electrically heated catalytic converter that warms up quickly after starting. The computer thinks the one on bank 1 is not cleaning the exhaust well enough.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Faulty catalyst heater or its circuit

checks: Check for catalyst heater codes and fix those first
Compare upstream and downstream O2 sensor readings
fix: Usually repairing the catalyst heater circuit or replacing the converter.

title: Heated Catalyst Temperature Below Threshold (Bank 1)
plain: The electrically heated catalytic converter on bank 1 is not getting as hot as it should after a start.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Catalyst heater relay, fuse or wiring fault

checks: Check the catalyst heater fuse, relay and wiring
Check the heater element resistance
fix: Usually repairing the heater circuit or replacing the heated converter.

title: Catalyst Temperature Sensor (Bank 1)
plain: The computer sees a problem with the sensor that measures catalytic converter temperature on bank 1. These sensors are mostly found on diesels and some turbo gas engines.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the vehicle drives
checks: Compare the sensor reading with other exhaust temperature sensors when the engine is cold
Inspect the sensor wiring for heat damage near the exhaust
fix: Usually a new catalyst temperature sensor or a wiring repair.

title: Catalyst Temperature Sensor Range/Performance (Bank 1)
plain: The bank 1 catalyst temperature sensor gives readings that do not fit how the engine is running.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the vehicle drives
checks: Compare the sensor reading with other exhaust temperature sensors when the engine is cold
Inspect the sensor wiring for heat damage near the exhaust
fix: Usually a new catalyst temperature sensor.

title: Catalyst Temperature Sensor Low Input (Bank 1)
plain: The bank 1 catalyst temperature sensor signal is lower than it should ever be.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the vehicle drives
checks: Compare the sensor reading with other exhaust temperature sensors when the engine is cold
Inspect the sensor wiring for heat damage near the exhaust
fix: Replace the sensor or repair the shorted wiring.

title: Catalyst Temperature Sensor High Input (Bank 1)
plain: The bank 1 catalyst temperature sensor signal is higher than it should ever be, often from an open wire.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the vehicle drives
checks: Compare the sensor reading with other exhaust temperature sensors when the engine is cold
Inspect the sensor wiring for heat damage near the exhaust
fix: Replace the sensor or repair the wiring.

title: Catalyst Heater Control Circuit (Bank 1)
plain: The computer sees an electrical fault in the circuit that powers the heater for the bank 1 catalytic converter, on vehicles that have one.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives

causes.name: Blown fuse or failed heater relay

checks: Check the fuse and relay for the catalyst heater
Measure heater resistance and check the wiring
fix: Usually a fuse, relay or wiring repair, or a new heated converter.

title: Catalyst Temperature Sensor Circuit (Bank 1 Sensor 2)

fix: Usually a new temperature sensor or a wiring repair.

checks: Compare the sensor reading with other exhaust temperature sensors when the engine is cold

fix: Usually a new temperature sensor.

fix: Replace the sensor or repair the shorted wiring.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation "A" Control Stuck Open
plain: The computer thinks the EGR valve is stuck open, letting exhaust into the engine when it should not. This can cause rough running and is most often seen on diesels.
symptoms: Rough idle, stalling or lack of power

causes.name: EGR valve stuck open from carbon or soot
Failed EGR valve motor or position sensor
Wiring fault to the EGR valve

checks: Command the EGR valve closed with a scan tool and watch actual position
Remove and inspect the valve for carbon or soot
fix: Usually cleaning or replacing the EGR valve.

title: Exhaust Gas Recirculation "A" Control Stuck Closed
plain: The computer thinks the EGR valve is stuck closed and cannot open when needed, which raises combustion temperatures and emissions.

causes.name: EGR valve stuck closed from carbon or soot
Failed EGR valve motor or position sensor
Wiring fault to the EGR valve

checks: Command the EGR valve open with a scan tool and watch actual position
Remove and inspect the valve for carbon or soot
fix: Usually cleaning or replacing the EGR valve.

title: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detection Reference Orifice Low Flow
plain: Some fuel vapor systems use a small pump with a tiny calibrated hole to test for leaks. The computer sees less air flowing through that reference hole than it should, which usually means it is blocked.
symptoms: No change in how the car drives
Other EVAP codes may set at the same time

causes.name: Reference orifice or filter clogged with dirt or debris
Blocked vent hose or canister filter
Wiring problem to the pump module

checks: Inspect the vent hose and canister filter for dirt, water or bugs
Run the EVAP leak test with a scan tool and watch pump pressure readings
fix: Usually a new leak detection pump module, sometimes with the charcoal canister.

cost.job: Replace EVAP leak detection pump module

examples: Often seen on Toyota and Lexus models that use a canister-mounted leak detection pump

title: Evaporative Emission System Leak Detection Reference Orifice High Flow
plain: The computer sees more air flowing through the leak test reference hole than it should, which usually means the leak detection pump or its valve is faulty.
symptoms: No change in how the car drives
Other EVAP codes may set at the same time

causes.name: Leaking hose or seal at the pump module
Wiring problem to the pump module

checks: Inspect hoses at the pump module for cracks or loose fittings
Run the EVAP leak test with a scan tool and watch pump pressure readings
fix: Usually a new leak detection pump module.

cost.job: Replace EVAP leak detection pump module

examples: Often seen on Toyota and Lexus models that use a canister-mounted leak detection pump
